title: Screen flows and user experience
objectives: Define a screen Flow as a user-interactive type that uses screens, choices, and supported distribution methods—and does not support Wait elements.
Design screens that collect required fields, validate user input on the screen, and show fault messages when DML fails.
Choose when a screen Flow is the UX versus a validation rule, formula field, approval process, autolaunched Flow, or Apex.
Wire record context with a Text input named recordId when a Flow action launches the screen.
diagnostic_question: Sales wants a guided form on the Account page to create a Contact with required Last Name and Email, show a friendly error if create fails, and not use a full LWC. Before reading, which flow type, screen settings, and fault path would you choose, and why not a validation rule alone?
definition: A screen Flow guides users through a business process launched from a supported distribution method. It requires user interaction because it includes screens, local actions, steps, choices, or dynamic choices, and it does not support Wait elements. Help tells you to use screen flows to build online forms that collect or display information for internal and external users. ([Flow Types](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_concepts_type.htm); [Build a Flow](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_build.htm); [Creating Records with Required Field Validation Example](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.automate_flow_build_example_required_fields.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers distinguish a screen Flow (a person clicks Next) from record-triggered automation, from a validation rule that only blocks a standard save, and from Apex or LWC. Missing required screen components, skipping fault paths, or forgetting recordId on a Flow action are the usual production bugs.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a hotel front desk. A screen Flow is the clerk walking a guest through a registration card: required fields, a progress indicator, and a polite error if the key packet cannot be created. A validation rule is the fire-code that refuses an illegal guest card on the standard record page. A formula is the always-printed room rate on the folio. An approval is the night manager's signature. Autolaunched Flow is the back-office key encoder that needs no clerk. Apex is a custom locksmith when the desk card cannot do the job.
deeper_explanation: Flow Types: Screen Flow guides users and is distributed via Flow actions, Lightning pages, Experience Builder, custom Aura/LWC, custom buttons or links, Flow Orchestration, web tabs, direct URLs, Visualforce, Lightning Out, and Embedded Service. It requires interaction and does not support Wait. Choice resources are a screen-flow resource type. ([Flow Types](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_concepts_type.htm))

Build a Flow / Use Screen Flows to Interact with Users: build online forms that collect or display information. Add a Screen element, configure components, and connect in auto-layout. Help's required-field example: mark Last Name and Email required on the screen, use Create Records, add a fault path with a Message component using the running interview's Fault Message, and optionally a Decision for complex validation logic. Consider Quick Actions when you want Flow Builder to indicate required fields automatically. ([Required Field Validation Example](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.automate_flow_build_example_required_fields.htm); [Build a Flow](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_build.htm))

Which-tool Help: a screen Flow starts when a user clicks Next on a form or a quick action that opens a form. That is different from a record-triggered start. Flow actions pass only the record Id into a Text input named recordId. Lightning App Builder does not pass collection or record variables and caps text inputs at 4,000 characters. ([Which automation tool](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.process_which_tool.htm); [Flow Variable Considerations](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_considerations_feature_variable.htm))

Screen-level requiredness and input validation improve data quality before DML; they do not replace object validation rules that must refuse illegal saves from API and Data Loader too. Approvals still own human routing. Apex remains complementary for CPU-intensive or Batch volume work, not for a three-field intake form.
Reactivity, stages/progress indicators, and Lightning versus Classic runtime are neighboring Help topics. Do not invent unsupported Wait on a screen Flow. Do not claim unofficial component limits.

mental_model.analogy: A hotel front desk: the screen Flow is the clerk and registration card; autolaunched Flow is the back-office encoder; validation is fire-code on the legal guest record; formula is the printed rate; approval is the night manager.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: A screen Flow is a guided form that needs a person. No Wait elements. Mark required fields on the screen, add a fault path, and use recordId for Flow actions. Validation still owns API-wide illegal saves. Apex is not the default intake form.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I pick Screen as the type because the user must interact. I distribute via action, Lightning page, or URL per Flow Types. I mark required components so Create Records does not hit REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING, and I add a fault path with Fault Message. Screen validation is UX; object validation rules still block Data Loader. Approvals remain a different product. I only call Apex if Help's complementary reasons apply.

when_to_use: Use a screen Flow when a person must walk through an online form to collect or display information, including on a record page or Experience site.
Use required screen components and a fault path when Create Records should not fail silently with REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING.
Use a Flow action plus recordId when the form must know the current record without Apex.
Use a validation rule in addition when illegal values must also be refused from API and Data Loader, not only the screen.
Use an approval process when a manager must decide, and Apex only if the form's logic is CPU-intensive beyond Flow.
when_not_to_use: Do not use a screen Flow when no user is present—that is autolaunched, record-triggered, or scheduled Flow.
Do not use a screen Flow as the only control if a validation rule must block every save channel.
Do not use a screen Flow to replace a formula field that should always calculate on the record.
Do not use a screen Flow as a substitute for an approval process work item.
Do not start in Apex or LWC for a three-field intake Help's screen Flow example already covers.

interview_questions.question: What is a screen Flow, and when do you choose it?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: It is the Flow type that requires a person to complete screens. You choose it for an online form, not for background automation, not as a validation rule, and not as the default Apex UI.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I cite Flow Types: screens, choices, no Wait, and the distribution list. I start it from Next or a quick action per which-tool Help. I still keep object validation for API channels and approvals for human routing. AUTO-003 record-triggered paths are the wrong type if a clerk must click.
interview_questions.example: LAB_CreateContact screen Flow on the Account page versus an after-save Task Flow with no form.
follow_ups: Can it run in Experience Cloud?
weak_answer_warnings: Calling every Flow a screen Flow

interview_questions.question: How do you prevent REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING in a create form?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Mark those fields required on the Screen components, then Create Records. Help also mentions Quick Actions to indicate required fields and Decision elements for complex logic.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I identify required fields first. I do not start in Apex. I add a fault path because other errors still happen. I add object validation if Data Loader must also block. A formula field cannot collect the input.
interview_questions.example: Last Name and Email required on LAB_CreateContact.
follow_ups: What goes on the fault screen?

interview_questions.question: The Flow action opens but AccountId is blank. Diagnose.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Check for a Text input named recordId that is available for input. Flow actions pass only that Id. App Builder will not pass a record variable.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I debug. I do not write Apex to 'fix' the Id. I Get Records after recordId if I need more fields. I do not confuse this with a validation rule.
weak_answer_warnings: Assuming all Account fields are passed

interview_questions.question: Users see a generic error when create fails. What is missing?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A fault path on Create Records with a Screen Message bound to the running interview Fault Message, as in Help's example.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I add the fault path and optionally loop back to the first screen if the user can fix inputs. I do not replace this with a validation rule error on a page they are not using. Apex try/catch is not the first UX.
interview_questions.example: Duplicate-rule failure showing Fault Message on LAB_CreateContact.
follow_ups: Should you log to a custom object?

interview_questions.question: When is a screen Flow the wrong tool?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When no user is present, when a formula should always calculate, when a validation rule must block every channel, when a person must approve, or when Help's complementary Apex cases apply.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Background work is autolaunched or record-triggered (AUTO-003/005). Approvals are Flow Approval Processes or Classic. I will not hide a hard data rule only on a screen the API never hits.
interview_questions.example: Data Loader inserting Contacts must still hit validation.
follow_ups: Could a screen launch an approval?

interview_questions.question: How do you distribute a screen Flow?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Flow Types lists actions, Lightning pages, Experience Builder, custom components, buttons, orchestration, tabs, URLs, Visualforce, Lightning Out, Embedded Service. Pick the lobby that matches the user.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I match internal vs external. I respect App Builder input limits. I do not distribute an autolaunched flow as if it had screens. recordId is for actions; URLs can set other inputs carefully (no currency merge fields).
interview_questions.example: Experience site form vs internal Account action.
weak_answer_warnings: One URL for every audience without a plan

interview_questions.question: Choice resource will not save on your autolaunched child. Why?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Choices are a screen-flow resource type. Autolaunched no-trigger flows do not support choices. Keep choices on the parent screen Flow and pass a Text or Id into the child.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not convert the child to Apex to store a picklist. I do not use a validation rule as a choice list. Subflow input names stay at or under 40 characters (AUTO-002).
interview_questions.example: Parent LAB_ScreenFlow passing LAB_Reason text into an autolaunched subflow.

interview_questions.question: Hotel-desk analogy, then break it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The screen Flow is the clerk and card; autolaunched is back office; validation is fire-code; formula is the printed rate; approval is the night manager. It breaks because API guests never visit the desk, so screen requiredness is not enough.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I add recordId as the reservation number the action hands over, and Fault Message as the 'key encoder failed' script. Apex is a locksmith for CPU/volume, not for three fields. No labeled-drawer story.
